title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with cheese, made with oil

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet or scrambled egg with cheese is a dish made from beaten eggs mixed with milk or cream, cooked in vegetable oil and finished with grated cheese. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, B‑vitamins and minerals, while cheese adds calcium and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs were first domesticated over 6,000 years ago in Southeast Asia.
Cheese in an omelet boosts calcium content to about 150 mg per serving.
Cooking with oil creates a pleasant aroma, but the oil should not be overheated to avoid trans‑fat formation.
Around the world omelets vary: French add herbs, Japanese include soy sauce, Americans often add bacon.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A two‑egg omelet provides roughly 12 g of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2) and folate, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Grated cheese adds calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Vegetable oil contributes monounsaturated fats that can support heart health when used in moderation.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Egg yolk contains lutein and zeaxanthin, which help protect the eyes from age‑related changes.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white proteins.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolk contains cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should monitor yolk intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: An oil‑fried, cheese‑topped omelet can be calorie‑rich (about 300 kcal per serving).

items.title: Trans‑fat formation when oil is overheated
items.content: Overheating vegetable oil may produce trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat eggs with a splash of milk, season with salt and pepper. Heat 1‑2 tsp of vegetable oil in a skillet, pour in the egg mixture, and when it begins to set, sprinkle grated cheese and gently fold until cooked through. Serve hot.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared omelet is best eaten immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat with a little extra oil to prevent dryness.
